questions.q: Translate: 'By 2050, people will have rejected filters.'
questions.a: Para 2050, la gente habrá rechazado los filtros.

questions.q: Translate: 'Without social media, standards would have changed less.'
questions.a: Sin las redes sociales, los cánones habrían cambiado menos.

days.guide: Discuss ¿Quién define la belleza? for 10 minutes, comparing your culture with one Spanish-speaking culture.

questions.q: Give an opinion with the subjunctive.
questions.a: Example: No creo que los medios deban decidir qué es bello.

days.guide: Your child writes the blog post; give the perfect-tenses quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Para el viernes, yo habría terminado el proyecto.' (meaning 'will have finished')
questions.a: Para el viernes, yo habré terminado el proyecto.

weeks.assessment_key: Blog post rubric (250 words, argumentative): 4 = clear thesis on beauty standards, two reasons with evidence from the article/ads, counterargument, persuasive conclusion, accurate grammar including 2+ perfect tenses; 3 = minor errors; 2 = weak argument; 1 = incomplete. Quiz sample key: 1) terminar/yo (fut. perf.) — habré terminado 2) cambiar/ellos (cond. perf.) — habrían cambiado 3) hacer/nosotros — habremos hecho / habríamos hecho 4) 'By 2030 standards will have changed' — Para 2030 los cánones habrán cambiado 5) 'I would have said the truth' — Habría dicho la verdad.

weeks.prep: Assemble a review packet on subjunctive (present, imperfect, adjective and adverbial clauses), perfect tenses, and passive voice. Choose an authentic reading and a listening passage with multiple-choice questions, a persuasive essay prompt with sources, and a cultural comparison prompt.
misconceptions: Choosing the subjunctive by keyword alone: check meaning (doubt vs. certainty, known vs. unknown antecedent, future vs. habitual).
Running out of time in simulated conversations: answer each prompt fully and quickly, using fillers rather than silence.

days.guide: Your child completes the mixed grammar review; reteach any category below 80%.

questions.q: Fill in: Era necesario que nosotros ___ (salir) temprano.
questions.a: saliéramos

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive with ser: 'Frida Kahlo pintó el cuadro Las dos Fridas.'
questions.a: El cuadro Las dos Fridas fue pintado por Frida Kahlo.

days.guide: Practice an authentic reading and a listening passage with multiple-choice questions; review strategies.

questions.q: What should you read before listening to an audio?
questions.a: The introduction and the questions, so you know what to listen for.

days.guide: Practice a 5-turn simulated conversation with 20-second responses.

questions.q: Respond: '¿Qué te gustaría hacer este verano y por qué?'
questions.a: Example: Me gustaría trabajar como voluntario en un campamento porque me encanta ayudar a los niños.

days.guide: Give the semester exam part 1: reading, listening, and grammar.

questions.q: Fill in: Cuando llegamos, la película ya ___ (empezar).
questions.a: había empezado

days.guide: Give part 2: persuasive essay and recorded cultural comparison.

questions.q: Translate: 'Although some think the opposite, I believe that...'
questions.a: Aunque algunos piensan lo contrario, creo que...

weeks.assessment_key: Semester exam: grammar sample key — 1) Dudo que tenga razón 2) Buscaba un libro que fuera fácil 3) Cuando llegue, te llamaré 4) Habíamos comido 5) Habré terminado 6) La casa fue construida en 1900 7) Se hablan muchos idiomas. Reading/listening keyed to chosen texts. Essay: 4 = thesis, sources cited, counterargument, accurate grammar; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = weak; 1 = incomplete. Cultural comparison: 4 = both cultures compared with examples, organized, accurate.

weeks.prep: Find a Spanish article comparing education in Spain and Mexico, the UC or CSU Spanish-language admissions page, and an article on free public universities in Argentina (e.g., the Universidad de Buenos Aires). Prepare a three-column comparison chart. Chart real si clauses: si + present → future, present, or command.
misconceptions: Using the future after si (*Si estudiaré, aprobaré): Si estudio, aprobaré.
False friends: 'el colegio' usually means a K–12 school, not college; 'la facultad' = a university school/department; 'la carrera' = degree program/major; 'la matrícula' = enrollment or tuition.
Equating 'bachillerato' with a bachelor's degree: in Spain and Mexico it is the final stage of secondary school (like 11th–12th grade); a bachelor's is 'la licenciatura' or 'el grado'.

days.guide: Your child compares Spain, Mexico, and the U.S. in a chart: stages, ages, exit exams, university access, cost.

questions.q: What is the 'bachillerato' in Spain?
questions.a: The two-year, non-compulsory upper-secondary stage (ages 16–18) after the ESO, which prepares students for the university entrance exam (often called la Selectividad, now PAU/EBAU).

questions.q: What are 'primaria', 'secundaria', and 'preparatoria' in Mexico?
questions.a: Elementary school (6 years), lower-secondary (3 years), and upper-secondary/high school (3 years, also called bachillerato).

days.guide: Teach si + present → future; your child writes 15 sentences about plans.

questions.q: Translate: 'If I get a scholarship, I will study engineering.'
questions.a: Si consigo (recibo) una beca, estudiaré ingeniería.

questions.q: Translate: 'If you have questions, call the university.'
questions.a: Si tienes preguntas, llama a la universidad.

days.guide: Read the article on Argentina's free public universities; your child summarizes it in 6 sentences.

questions.q: What is distinctive about public universities in Argentina?
questions.a: Undergraduate study at national public universities is tuition-free (since 1949), with open or easy admission, which gives wide access but large classes and limited funding.

days.guide: Discuss college and career plans with you or a tutor for 10 minutes.

questions.q: Ask: 'What would you like to study and why?'
questions.a: ¿Qué te gustaría estudiar y por qué?

days.guide: Your child writes the 200-word paragraph on future education plans.

questions.q: Correct: 'Si yo voy a la universidad, estudiaré medicina y seré médico.' (Is it correct?)
questions.a: Yes — si + present (voy) with the future (estudiaré, seré) is correct.

weeks.assessment_key: Paragraph rubric (200 words, future education plans): 4 = specific plans (school, major, how to pay), 4+ si clauses and future verbs, comparison with another country's system, accurate; 3 = minor errors; 2 = vague or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find a sample Spanish CV (currículum vitae/hoja de vida) and Spanish job ads (InfoJobs, Computrabajo, or bilingual U.S. postings). Make cards for 30 career terms. Print a formal cover letter model (carta de presentación).
misconceptions: Using an article after ser with professions (*Quiero ser un enfermero): Quiero ser enfermero.
Using 'aplicar' for applying to a job: standard Spanish uses 'solicitar un puesto' or 'postularse' (Latin America).
Mixing tú and usted in a cover letter or interview: use usted consistently.

days.guide: Teach 30 career terms; your child matches job ads to candidate profiles.

questions.q: Give the Spanish for nurse, lawyer, accountant, and interpreter.
questions.a: el/la enfermero/a, el/la abogado/a, el/la contador/a (contable in Spain), el/la intérprete

questions.q: What does 'jornada parcial' mean?
questions.a: Part-time.

days.guide: Your child writes a one-page Spanish CV.

questions.q: How do you write 'Volunteer at the public library (2024–present)'?
questions.a: Voluntario/a en la biblioteca pública (2024–actualidad).

days.guide: Your child writes a formal cover letter for a bilingual job.

questions.q: Write a sentence stating why you are a good candidate.
questions.a: Example: Considero que soy un buen candidato para este puesto porque soy bilingüe, responsable y tengo experiencia trabajando con el público.

days.guide: Role-play a job interview using usted; you ask 8 questions.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Cuáles son sus puntos fuertes?'
questions.a: Example: Soy organizado, aprendo rápido y me comunico bien en inglés y en español.

days.guide: Collect the CV and cover letter; give feedback using the rubric.

questions.q: Give a formal closing for a cover letter.
questions.a: Agradezco su atención y quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente, (nombre)

weeks.assessment_key: CV and cover letter rubric: CV — 4 = complete sections (datos personales, perfil, formación, experiencia, habilidades, idiomas), consistent format, accurate Spanish; Cover letter — 4 = formal greeting (Estimado/a señor/a...:), position named, 2–3 qualifications with examples, request for interview, formal closing (Atentamente), usted throughout; 3 = minor errors; 2 = missing sections or register errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find a Spanish article on Spain's long workday and the siesta myth (Spain uses Central European Time since 1940 though it lies geographically in the GMT zone; meals and work hours run late; surveys show most Spaniards do not take a daily siesta). Chart hypothetical si clauses: si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional. Prepare a free-time survey.
misconceptions: Using the conditional in the si clause (*Si tendría tiempo): Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría.
Thinking all Spaniards nap every day: the siesta is more myth than daily habit; long workdays with a long lunch break are the real pattern.
Translating 'If I was' with the indicative imperfect for hypotheticals (*Si era rico, viajaría): Si fuera rico, viajaría.

days.guide: Read the article; your child answers 10 comprehension questions.

questions.q: Why are Spanish schedules late compared to the sun?
questions.a: Since 1940 Spain has used Central European Time even though it lies geographically in the GMT zone, so clocks run ahead of the sun, and daily routines (lunch around 2–3 p.m., dinner around 9–10 p.m.) shifted late.

questions.q: Is the daily siesta common in Spain today?
questions.a: No; most Spaniards do not nap regularly — long workdays with a long lunch break are more typical.

days.guide: Teach hypothetical si clauses and compare with English 'If I were'; your child completes 15 transformations.

questions.q: Transform to hypothetical: 'Si tengo más tiempo, viajaré.'
questions.a: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría.

questions.q: Translate: 'If I were you, I would rest more.'
questions.a: Si yo fuera tú, descansaría más.

days.guide: Your child surveys five people about free-time habits and graphs results with Spanish labels.

questions.q: Ask: 'What do you do in your free time?'
questions.a: ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?

days.guide: Discuss ¿Qué harías si no tuvieras que trabajar? for 10 minutes; your child uses at least eight si clauses.

questions.q: Answer the question in one sentence.
questions.a: Example: Si no tuviera que trabajar, viajaría por Latinoamérica y aprendería a tocar la guitarra.

days.guide: Your child writes the cultural comparison; give the si-clause quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Si yo tendría dinero, compraría una casa.'
questions.a: Si yo tuviera dinero, compraría una casa.

weeks.assessment_key: Cultural comparison rubric (200 words): 4 = compares work hours, meal times, and leisure in Spain and the U.S. with evidence from the article and survey, uses comparison phrases and 2+ si clauses; 3 = minor errors; 2 = one-sided; 1 = incomplete. Quiz sample key: 1) Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría 2) Si fuéramos a España, comeríamos más tarde 3) Si pudiera, dormiría la siesta 4) ¿Qué harías si no tuvieras que trabajar? 5) Si gano, celebraré (real) vs. Si ganara, celebraría (hypothetical) 6) Si él supiera la verdad, se enojaría.

weeks.prep: Find career information in Spanish (e.g., Spain's SEPE employment site or a Latin American government site) and prepare slides software and note cards. Write the Unit 5 test (education/work vocabulary, real and hypothetical si clauses, an authentic listening passage).
misconceptions: Reading slides aloud: slides show key words and images; speak from note cards.
Switching to tú with the audience in a formal presentation: use ustedes and formal phrases (Buenos días a todos; A continuación...; Para concluir...).

days.guide: Your child researches a career's requirements, training, and salary in a Spanish-speaking country.

questions.q: Translate: 'To be a nurse in Spain you need a university degree.'
questions.a: Para ser enfermero/a en España se necesita un título universitario (un grado).

days.guide: Your child outlines a 4-minute presentation with intro, three points, and conclusion.

questions.q: Give three formal signposting phrases.
questions.a: En primer lugar..., A continuación..., Para concluir...

days.guide: Your child rehearses with note cards, records, and corrects pronunciation of difficult words.

questions.q: How do you pronounce 'requisito' and 'ingeniería'?
questions.a: re-ki-SI-to (qu = k, u is silent); in-he-nie-RÍ-a (g before e = Spanish j sound; stress on the í).

days.guide: Your child delivers the presentation and answers three unscripted questions.

questions.q: Ask an unscripted question.
questions.a: Example: ¿Qué es lo más difícil de esa profesión? / ¿Le gustaría trabajar en ese país? ¿Por qué?

days.guide: Give the Unit 5 test.

questions.q: Fill in: Si yo ___ (ser) intérprete, trabajaría en un hospital.
questions.a: fuera

weeks.assessment_key: Presentation rubric (4 minutes): 4 = researched career with requirements, training, and salary in a Spanish-speaking country, clear intro/3 points/conclusion, formal register, note cards only, answers 3 unscripted questions; 3 = minor issues; 2 = reads or short; 1 = incomplete. Unit 5 test sample key: 1) la beca = scholarship; el sueldo = salary; solicitar = to apply for; la formación = training/education; el requisito = requirement 2) Si estudio, aprobaré 3) Si tuviera tiempo, trabajaría 4) listening items keyed to the chosen passage.

weeks.prep: Find a BBC Mundo or UN en español article on Amazon deforestation and photos of the Amazon, Andean glaciers, and California drought. Make cards for 30 environmental terms. Set up a one-day household recycling and water audit sheet.
misconceptions: Using the indicative after expressions of will or urgency (*Es urgente que el gobierno actúa): Es urgente que el gobierno actúe.
Confusing 'el clima' (climate) with 'el tiempo' (weather) and 'la contaminación' covering all pollution types.
Using 'exigir' without a subject change: 'Exijo que las empresas reduzcan...' (different subjects).

days.guide: Teach 30 environmental terms; your child matches them to photos.

questions.q: Translate: 'The Andean glaciers are melting because of climate change.'
questions.a: Los glaciares andinos se están derritiendo por el cambio climático.

questions.q: What is 'la huella de carbono'?
questions.a: The carbon footprint — the greenhouse gases a person or activity produces.

days.guide: Read the article on Amazon deforestation; your child summarizes causes and consequences.

questions.q: What is the main cause of Amazon deforestation?
questions.a: Clearing land for cattle ranching, followed by agriculture (such as soy), illegal logging, mining, and fires.

questions.q: Give two consequences.
questions.a: Loss of biodiversity and Indigenous homelands, more carbon released into the atmosphere, and changes in regional rainfall.

days.guide: Your child writes 15 solutions with es urgente que, recomiendo que, and exijo que.

questions.q: Translate: 'It is urgent that we protect the forests.'
questions.a: Es urgente que protejamos los bosques.

questions.q: Translate: 'I demand that companies pay for their pollution.'
questions.a: Exijo que las empresas paguen por su contaminación.

days.guide: Your child audits household recycling and water use for a day and reports in Spanish.

questions.q: Report: 'Our family used 300 liters of water and recycled ten bottles.'
questions.a: Nuestra familia usó trescientos litros de agua y recicló diez botellas.

days.guide: Your child writes a 200-word letter to a local official recommending three actions.

questions.q: Write a formal opening for the letter.
questions.a: Estimado/a alcalde/alcaldesa: Le escribo para expresar mi preocupación por...

weeks.assessment_key: Recommendation letter rubric (200 words): 4 = formal greeting and closing, states the local problem, three specific actions with es urgente que/recomiendo que/sugiero que + correct subjunctive, evidence from the audit or article; 3 = minor errors; 2 = vague or register errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Gather graphs of California reservoir levels (California Department of Water Resources) and information on Mexico City's water supply (aquifer overuse, land subsidence, the Cutzamala system), plus an article on Chile's megadrought (central Chile, since about 2010). Prepare stakeholder role cards (farmer, city resident, environmentalist, mayor, water company).
misconceptions: Assuming drought is only about rainfall: overuse of groundwater, agriculture, and infrastructure matter (e.g., Mexico City is sinking because of aquifer overextraction).
Confusing 'el embalse' (reservoir) with 'la presa' (dam) and 'el acuífero' (underground aquifer).

days.guide: Your child interprets reservoir graphs and Mexico City supply data, answering questions in Spanish.

questions.q: Translate: 'The reservoir level dropped 20 percent compared to last year.'
questions.a: El nivel del embalse bajó un veinte por ciento en comparación con el año pasado.

questions.q: Why is Mexico City sinking?
questions.a: Because so much water is pumped from the aquifer beneath it, the ground compacts and subsides.

days.guide: Read about Chile's megadrought; your child identifies the author's point of view and evidence.

questions.q: What is the 'megasequía' in Chile?
questions.a: An unusually long drought affecting central Chile since about 2010, linked to climate change and worsened by heavy water use (agriculture, mining).

days.guide: Your child prepares a 2-minute oral comparison of water use in California and Chile.

questions.q: Write a comparison sentence.
questions.a: Example: Tanto en California como en Chile, la agricultura usa la mayor parte del agua, pero en Chile los derechos de agua son privados.

days.guide: Role-play a town meeting on water restrictions; each person represents a stakeholder.

questions.q: As a farmer, object politely.
questions.a: Example: Entiendo la situación, pero si reducen el riego, perderemos nuestras cosechas.

days.guide: Your child records the cultural comparison and self-assesses with the rubric.

questions.q: What does 'escasear' mean?
questions.a: To be scarce, to run short.

weeks.assessment_key: Recorded cultural comparison rubric (2 minutes): 4 = compares water use and policy in California and Chile with specific examples (agriculture, conservation rules, reservoirs), clear organization, comparison phrases, mostly accurate grammar; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = describes one place mainly; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find a PAHO/OPS (Organización Panamericana de la Salud) Spanish infographic on teen health and prepare a por/para chart. Gather information on the health systems of Cuba (universal, state-run), Spain (universal public Sistema Nacional de Salud funded by taxes), and the U.S. (mix of private insurance, employer plans, Medicare, Medicaid). Preview: topics may include mental health.
misconceptions: Using por for purpose/destination (*Estudio por ser médico): para (purpose, goal, recipient, deadline, destination) — Estudio para ser médico.
Using para for cause, duration, exchange, or through/by (*Gracias para la ayuda): Gracias por la ayuda; Caminamos por el parque; Lo compré por diez dólares.

days.guide: Your child analyzes the PAHO infographic and summarizes findings in 5 sentences.

questions.q: What is the OPS (PAHO)?
questions.a: The Pan American Health Organization, the World Health Organization's regional office for the Americas.

days.guide: Review por vs. para; your child completes 25 contextual sentences with reasons.

questions.q: Fill in: 'Hago ejercicio ___ estar sano y camino ___ el parque.'
questions.a: para; por

questions.q: Fill in: 'Gracias ___ la información; es muy útil ___ mi proyecto.'
questions.a: por; para

days.guide: Your child compares health systems in Cuba, Spain, and the U.S. in a chart.

questions.q: How is Spain's health system funded?
questions.a: Mainly through taxes; the national public system provides universal coverage, with optional private insurance.

days.guide: Your child writes a PSA script on a teen health issue (sleep, nutrition, mental health, vaping).

questions.q: Write a PSA line with a command and por/para.
questions.a: Example: Duerme ocho horas para tener energía; tu cuerpo te lo agradecerá por la mañana.

days.guide: Your child records the PSA; give the por/para quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Salimos por Los Ángeles mañana para la mañana.'
questions.a: Salimos para Los Ángeles mañana por la mañana.

weeks.assessment_key: PSA rubric: 4 = 1 minute, clear teen health message with facts from the infographic, commands and subjunctive (Es importante que...), por/para used correctly; 3 = minor errors; 2 = unclear; 1 = incomplete. Por/para quiz sample key: 1) Salgo para Madrid (destination) 2) Viajamos por Chile (through) 3) Este regalo es para ti (recipient) 4) Gracias por todo (cause) 5) Estudio para ser enfermera (goal) 6) Lo vendí por veinte dólares (exchange) 7) La tarea es para el lunes (deadline) 8) Estuve enfermo por una semana (duration) 9) Para un adolescente, habla muy bien (comparison) 10) Fue escrito por la OPS (agent in passive).

weeks.prep: Print a debate rubric and phrase list (estar a favor/en contra de, en mi opinión, no cabe duda de que, por un lado/por otro lado, refutar, sin embargo, ¿no crees que...?). Gather sources from Units 5–6 (environment, water, health). Arrange a debate partner (parent, tutor, or online language partner). Write the Unit 6 test (environment and health vocabulary; subjunctive of will, por/para).
misconceptions: Using subjunctive after 'no cabe duda de que' or 'es cierto que': they express certainty → indicative (No cabe duda de que el plástico contamina).
Personal attacks instead of rebuttals: refute the argument with evidence (Esa idea no tiene en cuenta que...).

days.guide: Your child chooses a resolution (e.g., Se deben prohibir los plásticos de un solo uso) and gathers evidence.

questions.q: Translate the resolution 'Single-use plastics should be banned.'
questions.a: Se deben prohibir los plásticos de un solo uso.

days.guide: Your child writes an opening statement and anticipates two counterarguments.

questions.q: Write an opening sentence.
questions.a: Example: Estoy a favor de prohibir los plásticos de un solo uso porque contaminan los océanos y dañan la salud.

days.guide: Practice debate phrases and timed rebuttals (30 seconds each).

questions.q: Rebut: 'Los plásticos son baratos y prácticos.'
questions.a: Example: Es cierto que son baratos, pero el costo ambiental es enorme y existen alternativas reutilizables.

days.guide: Hold and record the formal debate.

questions.q: Give a closing-statement opener.
questions.a: Para concluir, no cabe duda de que...

days.guide: Give the Unit 6 test.

questions.q: Correct: 'No cabe duda de que el plástico contamine el mar.'
questions.a: No cabe duda de que el plástico contamina el mar.

weeks.assessment_key: Debate rubric: 4 = clear opening statement with three evidence-based arguments, direct rebuttals, formal phrases, accurate grammar including subjunctive, closing statement; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = few rebuttals or frequent errors; 1 = cannot sustain. Unit 6 test sample key: 1) la sequía = drought; el embalse = reservoir; la huella de carbono = carbon footprint; prevenir = to prevent 2) Es urgente que reduzcamos el plástico 3) Recomiendo que bebas más agua 4) por/para items 5) No cabe duda de que el clima está cambiando.

weeks.prep: Print Horacio Quiroga's 'El almohadón de plumas' (1907, public domain) with a glossary. Obtain Jorge Luis Borges's 'Los dos reyes y los dos laberintos' (in El Aleph, 1949) from a library or licensed anthology — it is under copyright, so do not copy it. Preview: Quiroga's story is a horror tale about a slow, mysterious death.
misconceptions: Summarizing instead of analyzing: an analysis explains how the author creates an effect (suspense, irony, symbolism) with evidence.

Calling every strange story 'realismo mágico': Quiroga's tale is horror with a naturalistic explanation; Borges writes fantastic, philosophical fiction; magical realism (García Márquez) treats the supernatural as ordinary.
Writing about literature in the past only: use the literary present (Quiroga describe..., el rey abandona...).

days.guide: Read 'El almohadón de plumas' with the glossary; your child summarizes the plot in 8 sentences.

questions.q: Summarize the plot.
questions.a: Newlywed Alicia lives in a cold, silent house with her stern husband Jordán; she grows weak and anemic, has hallucinations, and dies; the maid notices stains on her feather pillow, and Jordán cuts it open to find a swollen parasite that had sucked her blood nightly.

days.guide: Analyze how Quiroga builds suspense (setting, gradual decline, doctors' failure, delayed revelation).

questions.q: How does the setting contribute to the mood?
questions.a: The white, silent, cold house (like an enchanted palace in autumn) mirrors the cold marriage and creates a chilling, isolated atmosphere.

questions.q: What is the effect of the final explanation about bird parasites?
questions.a: The clinical, matter-of-fact ending makes the horror seem real and possible, increasing its impact.

days.guide: Read Borges's story; discuss its symbolism.

questions.q: Summarize 'Los dos reyes y los dos laberintos'.
questions.a: A king of Babylon builds a complex labyrinth and traps a visiting Arab king in it to mock him; the Arab king escapes by praying to God, later conquers Babylon, and leaves the Babylonian king in the desert — a labyrinth with no stairs, doors, or walls — where he dies.

questions.q: What does the desert symbolize?
questions.a: A labyrinth made by God/nature, vaster than any human design; it suggests human pride is small before the divine and that cruelty is repaid.

days.guide: Your child compares the two endings in a Venn diagram.

questions.q: Give one similarity between the endings.
questions.a: Both end in death caused by something hidden or vast that the victim could not escape, and both reveal a final ironic twist.

days.guide: Your child writes a 250-word literary analysis paragraph on one story.

questions.q: Write a thesis for an analysis of Quiroga's story.
questions.a: Example: En 'El almohadón de plumas', Quiroga crea suspenso al retrasar la causa de la enfermedad de Alicia hasta el desenlace.

weeks.assessment_key: Literary analysis paragraph rubric (250 words): 4 = arguable thesis about technique or theme, 2–3 pieces of textual evidence (brief quotations or specific references) explained, literary vocabulary (el ambiente, el desenlace, el narrador, el símbolo), literary present, accurate; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = mostly summary; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Print José Martí's Versos sencillos I ('Yo soy un hombre sincero') and XXXIX ('Cultivo una rosa blanca') and Rubén Darío's 'Sonatina' (Prosas profanas, 1896) — all public domain. Obtain Gabriela Mistral's 'Los que no danzan' (from Ternura) from a library or licensed anthology; do not copy it. Queue a recording of 'Guantanamera', whose verses come from Martí.
misconceptions: Counting syllables by spelling: Spanish meter joins vowels between words (sinalefa) and adds a syllable when a line ends in a stressed word (aguda) or removes one when it ends in an esdrújula.
Thinking modernismo is the same as English 'modernism': Hispanic modernismo (Darío, c. 1888–1910) emphasized musicality, exotic and refined imagery, and art for art's sake.
Explicating by paraphrasing line by line: connect form (rhyme, meter, sound) to meaning and theme.

days.guide: Read Versos sencillos I and XXXIX aloud; your child marks the rhyme scheme and counts syllables, then listens to 'Guantanamera'.

questions.q: What is the meter and rhyme of 'Cultivo una rosa blanca'?
questions.a: Octosyllabic lines (8 syllables) in quatrains with abba rhyme (blanca/enero/sincero/franca).

questions.q: What is the message of 'Cultivo una rosa blanca'?
questions.a: The speaker offers the same white rose (kindness, peace) to the sincere friend and to the cruel person who hurts him — he answers cruelty with generosity, not with thistles or nettles.

days.guide: Read 'Sonatina'; your child lists images of color, luxury, and sound and identifies the modernista features.

questions.q: What is the situation in 'Sonatina'?
questions.a: A sad princess sits in her palace longing for something beyond her luxurious, confined life ('La princesa está triste... ¿qué tendrá la princesa?'); at the end her fairy godmother tells her a knight is coming on a winged horse to bring her love.

questions.q: What meter does Darío use?
questions.a: Alexandrines — 14-syllable lines divided into two halves of 7 (hemistiquios), giving a musical rhythm.

days.guide: Read a Mistral poem; learn that Gabriela Mistral (Chile) won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1945, the first Latin American to do so.

questions.q: What is 'Los que no danzan' about?
questions.a: It is a children's poem in which a child who cannot dance (because of disability or illness) is told she can dance with her heart; it invites everyone to join the dance of life.

days.guide: Your child memorizes and recites one stanza with expression.

questions.q: What should a good recitation do at the end of each line?
questions.a: Pause briefly only where punctuation or meaning requires, keeping the rhythm and linking vowels across words.

days.guide: Your child writes an explication of one poem in Spanish.

questions.q: Write a thesis for an explication of 'Cultivo una rosa blanca'.
questions.a: Example: En 'Cultivo una rosa blanca', Martí usa la imagen repetida de la rosa blanca para mostrar que el perdón y la generosidad son más fuertes que el odio.

weeks.assessment_key: Recitation rubric: 4 = memorized stanza, correct pronunciation and linking, expressive pauses at punctuation and line ends; 3 = minor slips; 2 = reads or hesitates; 1 = not prepared. Explication rubric (~250 words): 4 = identifies speaker, theme, and tone, analyzes 2–3 devices (rhyme, meter, imagery, metaphor, repetition) with quoted lines, explains how form supports meaning; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = mostly paraphrase; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Obtain Gabriel García Márquez's 'Un señor muy viejo con unas alas enormes' (1968) from a library anthology (under copyright; do not copy). Gather background on García Márquez (born 1927 in Aracataca, Colombia; Nobel Prize 1982; Cien años de soledad, 1967). Write a quiz on the story and past tenses.
misconceptions: Defining magical realism as fantasy: in magical realism, supernatural events appear in an otherwise realistic world and characters treat them as ordinary.
Assuming the townspeople honor the angel: they treat him as a curiosity and a source of profit, showing human cruelty and indifference.
Using the pluperfect where the preterite suffices: use había + participle only for an action before another past action.

days.guide: Read about García Márquez and Colombia; define magical realism with examples.

questions.q: What is 'el realismo mágico'?
questions.a: A literary style in which supernatural or impossible events occur in a realistic setting and are described as normal by the narrator and characters.

days.guide: Read the first half; your child annotates supernatural details treated as ordinary.

questions.q: How do Pelayo and Elisenda first react to the winged man?
questions.a: They are puzzled more than amazed, notice that he looks like a ragged old sailor, and a neighbor tells them he is an angel; they shut him in the chicken coop.

questions.q: Why does Father Gonzaga doubt the man is an angel?
questions.a: He does not understand Latin (the language of God's ministers) and looks too human and miserable; the priest writes to Church authorities for a ruling.

days.guide: Finish the story; discuss how the community treats the angel and what this reveals.

questions.q: How do Pelayo and Elisenda profit from the angel?
questions.a: They charge admission to see him and become rich enough to build a two-story mansion.

questions.q: How does the story end?
questions.a: The angel survives, grows new feathers, and finally flies away; Elisenda watches until he disappears, relieved.

days.guide: Your child writes a 300-word magical realist story using preterite, imperfect, and pluperfect.

questions.q: Write a magical realist opening.
questions.a: Example: El martes amaneció lloviendo flores amarillas, y como siempre, mi abuela salió a barrerlas antes del desayuno.

days.guide: Give the quiz on the story and past tenses.

questions.q: Fill in: Cuando el ángel se fue volando, Pelayo y Elisenda ya ___ (construir) una casa de dos pisos.
questions.a: habían construido

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: 1) Pelayo and Elisenda find an old man with huge wings in their courtyard after days of rain 2) a neighbor woman says he is an angel 3) they keep him in a chicken coop and charge admission, and become rich 4) Father Gonzaga doubts he is an angel because he does not understand Latin 5) the crowds leave for a woman who was turned into a spider for disobeying her parents 6) his 'miracles' are strange or useless 7) at the end he grows new feathers and flies away, and Elisenda watches with relief. Grammar: encontraron (preterite), llovía (imperfect), había llovido (pluperfect). Creative story rubric (300 words): 4 = one supernatural element treated as ordinary, realistic setting, preterite/imperfect/pluperfect used correctly, vivid detail; 3 = minor errors; 2 = fantasy without realism or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Obtain Federico García Lorca's La casa de Bernarda Alba (1936) from a library; read Act I in advance. Choose a Spanish-language film: 'Coco' (PG) in Spanish, or clips of 'El laberinto del fauno' (rated R for graphic violence — preview and choose clips carefully). Chart reported speech: present → imperfect, preterite → pluperfect, future → conditional, command → imperfect subjunctive.
misconceptions: Not shifting tenses in reported speech: 'Tengo hambre,' dijo → Dijo que tenía hambre.
Reporting commands with the indicative (*Bernarda dijo que se callan): Bernarda les dijo que se callaran.
Forgetting to change pronouns and time words: hoy → ese día, mañana → al día siguiente, aquí → allí.

days.guide: Read Act I aloud by roles; discuss oppression and silence.

questions.q: What does Bernarda impose on her daughters after her husband's death?
questions.a: Eight years of mourning, shut inside the house, cut off from men and the outside world.

questions.q: Who is Pepe el Romano, and why does he matter in Act I?
questions.a: A young man of the village who is to court Angustias, the eldest daughter, who has inherited money; the other daughters, especially Adela, are jealous.

days.guide: Teach reported speech; your child converts 15 direct quotes (from the play or invented).

questions.q: Convert: Bernarda: '¡Silencio!' (command to her daughters)
questions.a: Bernarda les ordenó a sus hijas que se callaran (que guardaran silencio).

questions.q: Convert: Adela dijo: 'Me pondré el vestido verde.'
questions.a: Adela dijo que se pondría el vestido verde.

days.guide: Watch the film or clips with a viewing guide (characters, setting, conflict, themes, memorable scenes).

questions.q: In 'Coco', what is the role of the ofrenda in the story?
questions.a: Photos on the family ofrenda allow the dead to cross over to visit on Día de Muertos; being remembered keeps a person alive in the Land of the Dead.

days.guide: Your child writes a 250-word film review using reported speech and opinion phrases.

questions.q: Write a sentence reporting what a character said.
questions.a: Example: Miguel le dijo a su familia que quería ser músico.

days.guide: Your child presents the review orally in 2 minutes.

questions.q: Give a recommendation phrase.
questions.a: Recomiendo esta película a quien le guste... / Les aconsejo que la vean porque...

weeks.assessment_key: Film review rubric (250 words): 4 = summary without spoilers, analysis of characters/themes/cinematography, opinion phrases, 3+ correct reported-speech sentences, recommendation; 3 = minor errors; 2 = mostly summary; 1 = incomplete. Oral presentation (2 minutes): 4 = clear, fluent, accurate.

weeks.prep: Collect the unit's texts (Quiroga, Borges, Martí, Darío, Mistral, García Márquez, Lorca) and a comparative essay outline. Print a peer/parent revision checklist. Write the Unit 7 test (literary vocabulary, reported speech, past tenses, a short unseen passage or poem).
misconceptions: Choosing texts with no real common ground: pick two that share a clear theme (death, power, confinement, identity, cruelty to outsiders).
Dropping long quotations without explaining them: introduce, quote briefly, and explain how the quote supports the thesis.
Retelling plots: the essay must compare how each author treats the theme.

days.guide: Your child chooses two texts sharing a theme and writes a working thesis.

questions.q: Give a theme shared by 'El almohadón de plumas' and La casa de Bernarda Alba.
questions.a: Confinement and oppression in a cold, controlling household leading to death (Alicia's isolation; the daughters' imprisonment under Bernarda).

days.guide: Your child gathers six quotations or specific references and explains each in Spanish.

questions.q: How do you introduce a quotation in Spanish?
questions.a: Como dice el narrador, "..."; Según Bernarda, "..."; El poeta escribe: "..."

days.guide: Your child writes a 400-word comparative literary essay.

questions.q: Write a comparative thesis.
questions.a: Example: Tanto Quiroga como Lorca muestran cómo un hogar opresivo destruye a las mujeres, pero Quiroga usa el terror mientras Lorca usa el silencio y la tensión dramática.

days.guide: Revise with the peer/parent checklist (thesis, evidence, explanation, tense, agreement, accents).

questions.q: Correct: 'En el cuento, Alicia se murió porque el animal la chupaba la sangre.' (literary present)
questions.a: En el cuento, Alicia muere porque el animal le chupa la sangre.

days.guide: Collect the final essay and give the Unit 7 test.

questions.q: Convert to reported speech: 'No entiendo latín,' dijo el cura.
questions.a: El cura dijo que no entendía latín.

weeks.assessment_key: Literary essay rubric (400 words): 4 = comparative thesis, organized by points of comparison, six brief quotations or specific references explained, literary vocabulary, accurate grammar in the literary present; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = summary-heavy or one text dominates; 1 = incomplete. Unit 7 test sample key: 1) el desenlace = ending/resolution; el ambiente = setting/atmosphere; el narrador = narrator; la estrofa = stanza 2) 'Vendré mañana,' dijo → Dijo que vendría al día siguiente 3) magical realism defined 4) Darío = modernismo; Mistral = Nobel 1945 5) passage items keyed to the text.

weeks.prep: Explore Calisphere (calisphere.org) photographs of ranchos, missions, braceros, and the UFW; find Spanish-language articles and oral histories (e.g., the Bracero History Archive). Prepare a long paper strip or a digital timeline tool.
misconceptions: Thinking California history begins with the Gold Rush: Indigenous peoples lived here for millennia, followed by the Spanish missions (1769), Mexican rule (1821–1848), and the Californio rancho era.
Thinking Californios kept their land after 1848: the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo promised property rights, but the Land Act of 1851, legal costs, and squatters caused many to lose their ranchos.
Confusing the Bracero Program with undocumented migration: braceros were legal contract workers recruited from Mexico (1942–1964).

days.guide: Read about the Californios and the rancho era; your child analyzes two Calisphere photos.

questions.q: Who were the Californios?
questions.a: Spanish-speaking residents of Alta California during the Spanish and Mexican periods, many of whom owned large cattle ranchos.

days.guide: Study the Bracero Program through Spanish-language oral histories.

questions.q: What was the Bracero Program?
questions.a: A U.S.–Mexico agreement (1942–1964) bringing millions of Mexican contract workers to U.S. farms and railroads; many faced low pay and poor conditions.

questions.q: Translate: 'My grandfather worked as a bracero in the fields of Salinas.'
questions.a: Mi abuelo trabajó como bracero en los campos de Salinas.

days.guide: Read about the UFW and Dolores Huerta's '¡Sí, se puede!'

questions.q: Who coined '¡Sí, se puede!' and when?
questions.a: Dolores Huerta, during a 1972 campaign in Arizona (during César Chávez's fast); it became the UFW's motto.

days.guide: Your child creates a bilingual timeline of Hispanic California history.

questions.q: Translate: 'In 1848 Mexico ceded California to the United States.'
questions.a: En 1848 México cedió California a los Estados Unidos.

days.guide: Your child presents the timeline orally.

questions.q: Give a cause-effect sentence.
questions.a: Example: Como los Californios no podían pagar los costos legales, muchos perdieron sus ranchos.

weeks.assessment_key: Timeline presentation rubric: 4 = 10+ accurate dated events from Indigenous California to the Chicano Movement, bilingual labels, explains causes/effects in Spanish with accurate past tenses, 3-minute presentation; 3 = minor errors; 2 = few events or errors; 1 = incomplete. Key facts: missions begin 1769; Mexican independence 1821; Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo 1848; Land Act 1851; Bracero Program 1942–1964; NFWA founded 1962; Delano grape strike 1965; East LA student walkouts 1968; '¡Sí, se puede!' 1972.

weeks.prep: Find a Univision or Telemundo local news segment and La Opinión (Los Angeles) articles. Help your child identify an adult Spanish speaker to interview, get permission to record, and choose a safe public or family setting.
misconceptions: Asking yes/no questions only: open questions (¿Cómo...? ¿Por qué...? Cuénteme sobre...) produce richer answers.
Using tú with an older interviewee you don't know well: use usted unless invited to use tú.
Transcribing word by word into English: transcribe in Spanish, then summarize.

days.guide: Watch a local Spanish-language news segment; your child summarizes one local story (qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, por qué).

questions.q: What does 'el reportaje' mean?
questions.a: A news report/feature story.

days.guide: Your child writes 12 interview questions about immigration, work, and traditions in usted form.

questions.q: Ask: 'When did you arrive in California?'
questions.a: ¿Cuándo llegó usted a California?

questions.q: Ask: 'What traditions do you keep from your country?'
questions.a: ¿Qué tradiciones mantiene de su país?

days.guide: Your child conducts and records the interview with permission.

questions.q: Ask permission to record.
questions.a: ¿Me permite grabar la entrevista? Solo la usaré para mi clase de español.

days.guide: Your child transcribes and summarizes key points in Spanish.

questions.q: Convert to reported speech: 'Llegué en 1995 y trabajé en un restaurante.'
questions.a: Dijo que había llegado en 1995 y que había trabajado en un restaurante.

days.guide: Your child writes a 300-word profile.

questions.q: Write an engaging first sentence.
questions.a: Example: Cuando la señora Rosa llegó a Los Ángeles en 1995, solo tenía una maleta y muchos sueños.

weeks.assessment_key: Interview profile rubric (300 words): 4 = engaging introduction, background, work, and traditions in accurate past and present tenses, 2–3 direct quotations and reported speech, respectful tone, conclusion with reflection; 3 = minor errors; 2 = list-like; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Set up a recording app or video editor (Audacity, GarageBand, or a phone editor). Help your child choose a theme from the year (identity, technology, art, environment, literature, California history) and find three authentic Spanish sources.
misconceptions: Writing a script too long for 5 minutes: about 650–750 spoken words fills 5 minutes.
Using copyrighted music or images without permission: use royalty-free music and credit image sources.

days.guide: Your child chooses a theme and format and writes a plan in Spanish.

questions.q: Translate: 'My podcast will explore how social media affects young people in Spain and the United States.'
questions.a: Mi pódcast explorará cómo las redes sociales afectan a los jóvenes en España y en Estados Unidos.

days.guide: Your child gathers three authentic sources and takes notes in Spanish.

questions.q: Name a reliable Spanish-language news source.
questions.a: Examples: BBC Mundo, El País, CNN en Español, Univision Noticias.

days.guide: Your child writes the script with intro, three segments, and conclusion.

questions.q: Write a podcast intro line.
questions.a: Example: ¡Bienvenidos a 'Voces jóvenes'! Hoy hablaremos de un tema que nos afecta a todos.

days.guide: Your child records audio/video and adds images or music.

questions.q: What should you check before recording?
questions.a: A quiet room, the microphone level, and a test recording; speak slowly and clearly.

days.guide: Your child edits and adds Spanish subtitles or show notes.

questions.q: Translate: 'In this episode we talk with...'
questions.a: En este episodio hablamos con...

weeks.assessment_key: Project checkpoint: 4 = theme chosen, three authentic sources noted, complete script with intro, three segments, and conclusion, raw recording done, editing started with subtitles/show notes; 3 = one stage behind; 2 = two stages behind; 1 = not started.

weeks.prep: Print the project and reflection rubrics and the ACTFL Intermediate Mid can-do statements. Gather the year's best work for the portfolio (essays, recordings, presentations, literary analysis, interview profile).
misconceptions: Self-assessing by feeling rather than evidence: tie each can-do statement to a specific piece of work.
Writing a reflection that lists activities: explain what you learned, how you improved, and what is still hard.

days.guide: Your child reviews the final cut and corrects language errors.

questions.q: Correct: 'Espero que el público disfruta el pódcast.'
questions.a: Espero que el público disfrute el pódcast.

days.guide: Your child presents the project and answers family questions in Spanish.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué fue lo más difícil del proyecto?'
questions.a: Example: Lo más difícil fue editar el audio, pero aprendí mucho.

days.guide: Your child self-assesses with ACTFL Intermediate Mid can-do statements, citing evidence.

questions.q: What can an Intermediate Mid speaker do?
questions.a: Handle everyday conversations, create with the language in connected sentences, ask and answer questions, and narrate in different time frames with some errors.

days.guide: Your child writes a 250-word reflection on the year's progress.

questions.q: Translate: 'If I had practiced more, I would speak more fluently.'
questions.a: Si hubiera practicado más, hablaría con más fluidez.

days.guide: Your child organizes a digital portfolio with labels and short Spanish descriptions.

questions.q: Write a portfolio caption.
questions.a: Example: Este ensayo argumentativo muestra mi uso de fuentes y del subjuntivo.

weeks.assessment_key: Project rubric: 4 = 5-minute product with accurate content from three sources, organized segments, varied grammar (subjunctive, si clauses, perfect tenses) with few errors, clear pronunciation, polished editing, answers questions in Spanish; 3 = minor issues; 2 = issues in several areas; 1 = incomplete. Reflection rubric (250 words): 4 = specific progress with examples, challenges, strategies, goals, accurate past/present/future; 3 = minor errors; 2 = general; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Assemble the final exam: a mixed grammar review set; an authentic reading and audio with multiple-choice questions; a persuasive essay prompt with three sources; a formal email to reply to; five simulated-conversation prompts (20 seconds each); and a cultural comparison prompt.
misconceptions: Mixing formal and informal register in the email reply: use usted throughout, a formal greeting and closing, and answer every question in the email.
Spending too long on one multiple-choice question: skip and return.

days.guide: Your child completes the mixed grammar practice set and reviews errors.

questions.q: Give: pluperfect yo of ver, conditional perfect ellos of hacer, imperfect subjunctive nosotros of tener.
questions.a: había visto, habrían hecho, tuviéramos

days.guide: Practice simulated conversations and a cultural comparison aloud.

questions.q: Respond: '¿Qué consejos le darías a un nuevo estudiante de español?'
questions.a: Example: Le aconsejaría que escuchara música en español y que no tuviera miedo de cometer errores.

days.guide: Give final exam part 1: reading and listening.

questions.q: What should you do if you don't know an answer?
questions.a: Eliminate clearly wrong choices, use context, make your best guess, and move on.

days.guide: Give part 2: persuasive essay with sources and a formal email reply.

questions.q: Write a formal email closing.
questions.a: Le agradezco de antemano su atención. Atentamente, (nombre)

days.guide: Give part 3: simulated conversation and 2-minute cultural comparison.

questions.q: Respond in 20 seconds: '¿Qué harás este verano para seguir practicando el español?'
questions.a: Example: Este verano leeré una novela en español y veré series con subtítulos en español.

weeks.assessment_key: Final exam: grammar sample key — 1) Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría 2) Dudo que lo sepa 3) Busco a alguien que hable francés 4) Habían salido 5) Fue construido por... 6) Dijo que vendría 7) por/para items. Interpretive items keyed to chosen texts. Essay rubric: 4 = thesis, all sources cited, counterargument, organized, accurate; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = weak; 1 = incomplete. Email rubric: 4 = answers all questions, asks for details, formal register throughout. Conversation and cultural comparison: 4 = full, relevant, fluent responses with varied grammar; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = short or inaccurate; 1 = minimal.
